solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: According to Spooner, presidential hopeful avoids large vehicles

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the two words found must trade their starts

blocks.note: Donald Trump, a candidate for the US presidency; his initial sound swaps with the next word's
to duck something is to dodge it

explanation.surface: A would-be president sidesteps some big lorries on the campaign trail.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUMP DUCKS, said with the opening sounds swapped, becomes DUMP TRUCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dump trucks are heavy tipper lorries used on building sites, so they are large vehicles.

clue.text: Losing head in idiotic fury, giving offence

indicators.note: losing its head means the phrase drops its very first letter

blocks.note: dumb means stupid
rage and fury are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone loses their head in a stupid fit of anger and offends people.
explanation.walkthrough: DUMB RAGE drops its first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbrage means resentment, as in 'take umbrage', the state of feeling offended, so it is offence.

clue.text: In which little kids go doolally

blocks.note: first meaning: a chamber pot used by toddlers being toilet trained
second meaning: British slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A place where small children go a bit crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like 'go doolally', going mad, but in the first meaning it is to relieve oneself. Doolally is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A potty is a child's toilet bowl, and potty also means slightly mad.

clue.text: Transport, a pain in the neck, observed taking hours

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the next item goes within

blocks.note: a rick is a sprain, as in a ricked neck
saw is the past tense of see, to observe
H is the abbreviation for hours

explanation.surface: Public transport described as a nuisance, watched as it takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pain in the neck' suggests a nuisance; here it is literal, a sprain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled vehicle pulled or pedalled to carry passengers, a form of transport.

clue.text: Soul icon recoils shocked, making track ending with a hit

definitions.text: making track ending with a hit

indicators.note: shocked letters are jolted out of their places and fall into a new order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A soul music legend is horrified that their recording finishes with a chart hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' and 'hit' suggest music; they mean a path and an impact.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision course is a path that will end in a crash, a track whose end is a hit.

clue.text: Characters in borders of South Tyrone travel in historical town

indicators.note: the borders of words are their outside edges, so only their end characters are taken

blocks.note: first and last letters of South
first and last letters of Tyrone, a county of Northern Ireland
first and last letters of travel

explanation.surface: Someone touring a border region of Northern Ireland, visiting an old town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders' suggests the Irish border; it is the edges of three words. Tyrone is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtetl was a small Jewish town in Eastern Europe before the Holocaust, now a historical type of settlement.

clue.text: Abroad, how are you getting wine?

blocks.note: first meaning: the French greeting ça va?, the foreign way of asking how someone is
second meaning: Spanish sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone overseas is asked how they are while being handed a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' signals a foreign phrase: in French, ça va? means 'how are you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is the sparkling white wine made in Catalonia in Spain by the traditional method.

clue.text: Business representative, with help, brought up clothing in French collections

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the word reads backwards
clothing something means wrapping it, so these pieces go around the French word

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a Member of Parliament represents a constituency
aid and help are synonyms
en is the French for in

explanation.surface: A sales rep, with a helper, raised garments in French fashion collections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collections' suggests fashion ranges; it is books of gathered material.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia, plural of compendium, are collections of works or information gathered into one volume.

clue.text: Maybe Czech knocked over houses along with old tribe

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, so the word reads backwards
a word that houses another holds it inside, like a home

blocks.note: Czechs are an example of a Slav people, hence 'maybe'
and means along with

explanation.surface: A Czech, perhaps, knocking down houses together with an ancient tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints destructive hooligans, which is the modern sense of the answer, but the definition wants the historical people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vandals were a Germanic people who sacked Rome in 455, an ancient tribe.

clue.text: Notice after passing on old coin

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A notice about some old money changing hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing on' looks like handing the coin over; it means dying. A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit, short for obituary, is the newspaper notice published after someone has died.

clue.text: Think of time to wear ring (round object)

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them
T is the abbreviation for time
the letter O is round in shape
to object to something is to mind it

explanation.surface: Musing on when to put on a ring, perhaps a wedding band, with an aside about its shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring takes on the time, so CALL is followed by T; then the bracketed words supply O and MIND.
explanation.definitionFit: To call to mind is to recall or remember, which is to think of something.

clue.text: Lecherous group of commandos grabbing car part reduced by 25%

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the noun: lecherous ones

indicators.note: cutting a quarter means a four-letter word loses one of its letters, here the last
a group grabbing something holds it inside itself

blocks.note: the Special Air Service, the British army's special forces regiment
a tyre is part of a car's wheel

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers lift part of a car that has been cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: A tyre has four letters, so removing 25% drops one of them. The SAS is Britain's Special Air Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs are the goat-like woodland spirits of Greek myth, proverbial for lust, so they are lecherous creatures.

clue.text: Hear twin's changed out of clothing

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a fresh order, as twins might change their outfits

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: News that a twin has got changed out of their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twin's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the raw is an idiom for naked, so it describes someone out of their clothing.

clue.text: Briefly tried cooked rabbit, one dish from Asia

indicators.note: made brief, the word is cut short by losing its last letter
cooked letters are mixed up and transformed like ingredients

blocks.note: tried shortened by one letter
to rabbit, as to yak, is to chatter on
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sampled cooked rabbit as an Asian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like the meat, but it is the British verb for chattering. 'Rabbit on' means talk at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese dish of meat or fish glazed with sweet soy sauce, so it comes from Asia.

clue.text: Taking off cap, taking off cap

indicators.note: removing the cap of a word means dropping its top, the first letter in this down entry

blocks.note: a cap is a limit, as in a spending cap

explanation.surface: A repetitive phrase that sounds like a hat being doffed twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The same three words are used twice: first as the definition and a synonym, then as an instruction to remove LIMITATION's first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A taking-off is a mimicking impersonation of someone, so it is an imitation.

clue.text: Husband in need of cheering up about career

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: someone sad needs cheering up
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband feels low about his job and needs a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun meaning job; it is the verb meaning to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to hurtle along at speed, which is to dash.

clue.text: Spot of trouble admitted by President Truman, at first

indicators.note: at first points to the very start of the word, so only its opening letter is used
something admitted by others is let in among them, so it goes inside

blocks.note: James K. Polk, the 11th US president
ado is fuss or bother
first letter of Truman

explanation.surface: A bit of trouble owned up to by President Truman early on.
explanation.walkthrough: The president is not Truman but another one, Polk; Truman just gives his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A polka dot is one of the round spots in a regular pattern on fabric, so it is a spot.

clue.text: Place to drink gin uncovered, or port

indicators.note: with its covering removed, the word keeps only what lies inside its outer letters

blocks.note: a bar is somewhere drinks are served
the middle letter of gin

explanation.surface: A choice between going to a bar for a neat gin or a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine beside the gin; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is a major seaport on the Adriatic coast of southern Italy.

clue.text: Erotic confession from Conservative I ignored

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: the phrase 'I am a Tory', a Conservative owning up
the letter to be dropped

explanation.surface: A racy admission from a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory means relating to sexual love, from Latin amare, to love, so it means erotic.

clue.text: Order one sent, packing article in recent deliveries?

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters take a new arrangement
packing something means holding it inside, so the shuffled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Ordering a package to be sent with an item among the latest deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests parcels; the question mark warns that these are babies just delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonates are newborn infants, and a birth is a delivery, so they are recent deliveries.

clue.text: Features in liberal papers penned by European? Certainly

indicators.note: penned means enclosed as in a pen, so these go inside what follows

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
yes, certainly
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
identity papers

explanation.surface: Stories in left-leaning newspapers written by a European? Of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' suggests newspaper articles, fitting the papers; it means parts of the face. The European and the 'Certainly' join first, then enclose the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelids are parts of the face, and features can mean the parts of a face.

clue.text: Right note lifted musical sound effect

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means raised upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a breve is a long musical note, equal to two semibreves

explanation.surface: The correct note was taken from a recording as an audio effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' could be any single letter A to G; it is a whole note name here.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is an echoing effect added to recorded music.

clue.text: German agreed with a single friend over something seedy and hot

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the words before it are read backwards

blocks.note: ja is German for yes
a pal is a friend
a single thing is one

explanation.surface: A German says yes to an only friend about some shady, sizzling business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A single friend' is reversed as a unit: ONE PAL read backwards. 'Seedy' looks like disreputable but means full of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalapeño is a hot chilli pepper full of seeds, so it is literally seedy and hot.

clue.text: Officer picked up the gist

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by ear, so the word is judged on how it is said

blocks.note: a colonel is a senior army officer, and the word is pronounced like a seed

explanation.surface: An officer has grasped the main point of a briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: The rank colonel is famously pronounced 'kernel' despite its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the central core of a nut, and figuratively the essential part of an argument.

clue.text: Drive back from spin around Portugal's capital

indicators.note: a capital is the head of something, so only the first letter is used
going around something means enclosing it

blocks.note: to reel is to whirl round
first letter of Portugal

explanation.surface: Driving away from a tour around Lisbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests Lisbon; it means the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an attack is to drive the attackers back.

clue.text: Was an autocratic boss denied more shifts?

indicators.note: the letters shift their places, ending up in a new order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Was a tyrannical manager refusing staff any extra shifts at work?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifts' reads as work periods a boss allocates; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to rule arrogantly over others, as a dictatorial boss does.

clue.text: Tips from professional astrologer involving Lion and Water Carrier

indicators.note: the tips of words are their ends, here the first letter of each

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Star-sign advice from an astrologer covering Leo and Aquarius.
explanation.walkthrough: Lion and Water Carrier look like the signs Leo and Aquarius; the second is literal, something to carry water in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket, a vessel for carrying water.

clue.text: Just cycling around in French city

indicators.note: cycling round moves letters from the front of the word to its back, keeping their sequence

blocks.note: just and only are synonyms, as in 'just a minute'

explanation.surface: Simply riding a bike around a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters move to the end: ON-LY becomes LY-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyon is France's third-largest city, at the meeting of the Rhône and Saône.

clue.text: What priests may do about broken heart, struggling for inspiration

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently
being about something means going round it, so this goes around the shuffled letters

blocks.note: priests bless their congregations
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Clergy praying over a heartbroken soul who searches for spiritual guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' looks spiritual, fitting the priests, but means breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration literally means drawing breath, so someone struggling for it is breathless.
